3	/// The menu bar's record indicator (road map 3, R1c), and since R2c the
4	/// recording's CONTROLS — the app's first `NSStatusItem`: a dot in
5	/// `DS.meterClip` and the elapsed time while a recording runs, a pause
6	/// glyph and the FROZEN time while it is paused, and a two-row menu that
7	/// reads Pause Recording · Stop Recording, then Resume Recording · Stop
8	/// Recording while paused. It exists because a global hotkey would need an
9	/// Input Monitoring or Accessibility grant, and because the recorder panel
10	/// is OFF SCREEN for the recording's whole span (decision 7: it orders out
11	/// at `recordingDidStart` whatever the source, and comes back only with
12	/// something to say) — so this item is the recording's whole chrome, and it
13	/// needs no grant and is reachable from every Space.
14	///
15	/// It is created when a recording starts and removed the moment the
16	/// recording ENDS — before the landing, not after it: once the recorder is
17	/// finishing there is nothing left for it to do. The label is pushed by its
18	/// owner's timer (`update(elapsed:paused:)` — the panel's at 30 Hz, the
19	/// tool's at 1 Hz), so this class keeps no timer and no recorder; it holds
20	/// three closures, `AudioNormalize`'s value-in-value-out posture applied to
21	/// a control, so a probe can make one without the panel. It never asks
22	/// whether a pause SUCCEEDED: the owner's next `update` says, by `paused`,
23	/// and that is the one place the menu is decided.
24	///
25	/// **The menu is rebuilt only when `paused` FLIPS, never per tick**, and
26	/// the rows are replaced inside the one `NSMenu` the item was shown with
27	/// rather than the menu swapped. A status item's menu may be OPEN when a
28	/// tick fires — the tracking run loop delivers the timer (below) — and a
29	/// title change under an open menu is harmless where rebuilding its rows
30	/// thirty times a second is not; the flip itself cannot arrive under the
31	/// open menu from the menu's own row, because a click closes the menu
32	/// before its action runs. `menuTitles(paused:)` and
33	/// `title(elapsed:paused:)` are PURE, which is how a probe pins both menus
34	/// and both labels without a menu bar.
35	///
36	/// **`freeze()` pins the mark from the owner's Stop on** (R2 review). The
37	/// owner's tick goes on calling `update` through its stopping phase, with
38	/// `paused` read off a phase that is `.stopping` and no longer `.paused`,
39	/// so a Stop from paused used to bring the coral dot back for the second or
40	/// two the finish takes — a recording that was not capturing, shown as
41	/// capturing. Frozen, `update` keeps the mark and the menu it last showed
42	/// and moves only the time; the panel calls it in `stopRecording()`, the
43	/// tool's chrome at its Stop. And `openMenu()` is a click on the button —
44	/// it pops the menu exactly as a person's click would — for the quit guard
45	/// while the panel is hidden (`RecorderPanelController.revealControls`), so
46	/// a person who paused and forgot is shown Pause, Resume and Stop rather
47	/// than beeped at.
48	///
49	/// **That timer runs in `.common` run-loop modes, and this item is why**
50	/// (R1 review). Opening a status item's menu runs the main run loop in
51	/// event-tracking mode for as long as the menu is down, and a timer
52	/// scheduled in the default mode alone does not fire there — so the elapsed
53	/// label froze at the moment its menu opened, which is the one moment a
54	/// person is looking at it to decide whether to press Stop. The panel adds
55	/// its tick (and its countdown, for the same reason) with
56	/// `RunLoop.main.add(_:forMode: .common)`, and `update(elapsed:paused:)` is
57	/// then called under the open menu as it is at any other time.
58	///
59	/// **One fixed length** (#98). The item is sized ONCE, `itemLength`: the
60	/// widest title either mark makes at `widestElapsed` (9:59:59) plus
61	/// `titleInset` each side, so the menu bar's other items never shift as the
62	/// seconds tick, the hour appears or the mark flips between the dot and
63	/// the pause glyph. A label past 9:59:59 is wider than that; it is not
64	/// sized for.
65	///
66	/// The fonts are the SYSTEM's, not `DS`'s: the menu bar is the OS's chrome
67	/// and a vendored face there would read as a foreign object. Monospaced
68	/// digits so the label does not jitter as the seconds tick. The pause
69	/// glyph takes NO colour of its own — the coral dot means "capturing", and
70	/// a paused recording is not — so it is drawn in whatever the menu bar
71	/// draws its text in, light or dark.
72	///
73	/// **While shortcuts record** (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-61; the
74	/// owner: a keyboard mark plus a menu row) — `keys`, from the recorder's
75	/// `recordsKeys` at construction — the title carries `keysGlyph` after the
76	/// dot or the pause glyph, in the menu bar's own colour, and the menu's first
77	/// row is a disabled `keysRow` and a separator, paused or not. The length is
78	/// fixed per item for the marks it shows (`itemLength(keys:)`), so an item
79	/// without shortcuts keeps the one length, title and menu it always had.
80	final class RecorderStatusItem: NSObject {
81	    /// Two heavy vertical bars (U+275A). The panel's footnote spells a pause
82	    /// with the same glyph, from here, so the two never drift apart.
83	    static let pauseGlyph = "❚❚"
84	    /// The keyboard (U+2328) with the text presentation selector, so the menu bar draws it in
85	    /// its own ink and never as an emoji (CU-61).
86	    static let keysGlyph = "⌨\u{FE0E}"
87	    /// The menu's first, disabled row while shortcuts record (CU-61).
88	    static let keysRow = "Recording keyboard shortcuts"
89	    /// The longest time the item is sized for (the type doc).
90	    static let widestElapsed: TimeInterval = 35_999
91	    /// Room each side of the title inside the item.
92	    static let titleInset: CGFloat = 6
93	    /// The item's one length: the wider of the two marks' titles at
94	    /// `widestElapsed`, rounded up, plus the insets (the type doc).
95	    static let itemLength: CGFloat = RecorderStatusItem.itemLength(keys: false)
96	
97	    /// The length for an item that shows the keyboard mark or not: the wider of the two marks'
98	    /// titles at `widestElapsed`, rounded up, plus the insets (CU-61).
99	    static func itemLength(keys: Bool) -> CGFloat {
100	        [false, true].map { paused in
101	            ceil(
102	                RecorderStatusItem.title(elapsed: widestElapsed, paused: paused, keys: keys)
103	                    .size().width)
104	                + 2 * titleInset
105	        }.reduce(0, max)
106	    }
107	
108	    /// Whether this item shows the keyboard mark and row: the recording records shortcuts.
109	    let keys: Bool
110	    private let onPause: () -> Void
111	    private let onResume: () -> Void
112	    private let onStop: () -> Void
113	    private var item: NSStatusItem?
114	    /// Which of the two menus the item shows. `update` compares `paused`
115	    /// with it before touching the menu (the type doc).
116	    private var menuShowsPaused = false
117	    /// Set by `freeze()`: `update` then reads its mark from `menuShowsPaused`
118	    /// and never from the argument.
119	    private var frozen = false
120	
121	    init(
122	        keys: Bool = false, onPause: @escaping () -> Void, onResume: @escaping () -> Void,
123	        onStop: @escaping () -> Void
124	    ) {
125	        self.keys = keys
126	        self.onPause = onPause
127	        self.onResume = onResume
128	        self.onStop = onStop
129	        super.init()
130	    }
131	
132	    @available(*, unavailable)
133	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
134	        fatalError("RecorderStatusItem does not support NSCoder")
135	    }
136	
137	    deinit { remove() }
138	
139	    /// Whether the item is in the menu bar.
140	    var isShowing: Bool { item != nil }
141	
142	    /// Puts the item up, at 0:00 with the RECORDING menu and its one fixed
143	    /// length for its marks. A second call while showing is a no-op.
144	    func show() {
145	        guard item == nil else { return }
146	        let item = NSStatusBar.system.statusItem(withLength: Self.itemLength(keys: keys))
147	        item.menu = NSMenu(title: "Recording")
148	        self.item = item
149	        menuShowsPaused = false
150	        frozen = false
151	        rebuildMenu(paused: false)
152	        item.button?.toolTip = Self.tooltip(paused: false)
153	        update(elapsed: 0, paused: false)
154	    }
155	
156	    /// The owner's timer calls this — 30 Hz from the panel, 1 Hz from the
157	    /// tool — with the recorder's `elapsed`, which freezes while paused, so
158	    /// a paused label holds still on its own. The menu and the tooltip are
159	    /// rebuilt only when `paused` differs from what they show; frozen, the
160	    /// argument is ignored and the mark stays (the type doc).
161	    func update(elapsed: TimeInterval, paused: Bool) {
162	        guard let item else { return }
163	        let paused = frozen ? menuShowsPaused : paused
164	        item.button?.attributedTitle = Self.title(elapsed: elapsed, paused: paused, keys: keys)
165	        guard paused != menuShowsPaused else { return }
166	        menuShowsPaused = paused
167	        rebuildMenu(paused: paused)
168	        item.button?.toolTip = Self.tooltip(paused: paused)
169	    }
170	
171	    /// From the owner's Stop on: the mark and the menu stay what they last
172	    /// were, whatever `update` is told (the type doc).
173	    func freeze() {
174	        frozen = true
175	    }
176	
177	    /// A click on the item's button, which pops its menu as a person's click
178	    /// would (the type doc); false with no item to click, which the caller
179	    /// answers with a beep.
180	    @discardableResult
181	    func openMenu() -> Bool {
182	        guard let button = item?.button else { return false }
183	        button.performClick(nil)
184	        return true
185	    }
186	
187	    func remove() {
188	        guard let item else { return }
189	        NSStatusBar.system.removeStatusItem(item)
190	        self.item = nil
191	    }
192	
193	    /// The rows of the menu the item already has, replaced in place: the
194	    /// first is Pause or Resume by `paused`, the second is always Stop; while
195	    /// shortcuts record, a disabled `keysRow` and a separator come first.
196	    private func rebuildMenu(paused: Bool) {
197	        guard let menu = item?.menu else { return }
198	        menu.removeAllItems()
199	        if keys {
200	            let row = NSMenuItem(title: Self.keysRow, action: nil, keyEquivalent: "")
201	            row.isEnabled = false
202	            menu.addItem(row)
203	            menu.addItem(.separator())
204	        }
205	        let actions = [
206	            paused ? #selector(resumeClicked(_:)) : #selector(pauseClicked(_:)),
207	            #selector(stopClicked(_:)),
208	        ]
209	        for (title, action) in zip(Self.menuTitles(paused: paused), actions) {
210	            let row = NSMenuItem(title: title, action: action, keyEquivalent: "")
211	            row.target = self
212	            menu.addItem(row)
213	        }
214	    }
215	
216	    @objc private func pauseClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
217	        onPause()
218	    }
219	
220	    @objc private func resumeClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
221	        onResume()
222	    }
223	
224	    @objc private func stopClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
225	        onStop()
226	    }
227	
228	    // MARK: - The vocabulary, pure
229	
230	    /// The rows, in order, the separator aside: `keysRow` first while shortcuts record. Pure, so
231	    /// a probe can pin every menu.
232	    static func menuTitles(paused: Bool, keys: Bool = false) -> [String] {
233	        (keys ? [keysRow] : []) + [paused ? "Resume Recording" : "Pause Recording", "Stop Recording"]
234	    }
235	
236	    /// The button's tooltip, which says which of the two states the item
237	    /// is showing.
238	    static func tooltip(paused: Bool) -> String {
239	        paused ? "Frame Job's recording is paused" : "Frame Job is recording"
240	    }
241	
242	    /// `m:ss`, and `h:mm:ss` past an hour. Pure, so a probe can pin it.
243	    static func label(for seconds: TimeInterval) -> String {
244	        let whole = Int(max(0, seconds.rounded(.down)))
245	        let hours = whole / 3600
246	        let minutes = (whole % 3600) / 60
247	        let secs = whole % 60
248	        if hours > 0 { return String(format: "%d:%02d:%02d", hours, minutes, secs) }
249	        return String(format: "%d:%02d", minutes, secs)
250	    }
251	
252	    /// The dot in `DS.meterClip` while recording, or the pause glyph in the
253	    /// menu bar's own colour while paused (the type doc), then, while
254	    /// shortcuts record, a space and `keysGlyph` in the menu bar's own colour,
255	    /// then the time in the menu bar's own face with monospaced digits.
256	    static func title(elapsed: TimeInterval, paused: Bool, keys: Bool = false)
257	        -> NSAttributedString
258	    {
259	        let size = NSFont.systemFontSize
260	        var mark: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [.font: NSFont.systemFont(ofSize: size)]
261	        if !paused { mark[.foregroundColor] = DS.meterClip }
262	        let title = NSMutableAttributedString(string: paused ? pauseGlyph : "●", attributes: mark)
263	        if keys {
264	            title.append(
265	                NSAttributedString(
266	                    string: " " + keysGlyph, attributes: [.font: NSFont.systemFont(ofSize: size)]))
267	        }
268	        title.append(
269	            NSAttributedString(
270	                string: " " + label(for: elapsed),
271	                attributes: [.font: NSFont.monospacedDigitSystemFont(ofSize: size, weight: .regular)]))
272	        return title
273	    }
274	}

1	import AVFoundation
2	import AppKit

4	/// One popup row as a hot-plug compares it: the id it carries (nil for
5	/// "None connected" and "Off") and its title.
6	struct HotPlugRow: Equatable {
7	    let id: String?
8	    let title: String
9	}
10	
11	/// Hot-plug (camera-recording CR2c, spec §11 CAM-8) —
12	/// `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s twelfth file, NEW rather than cut, as
13	/// `+Camera.swift` and `+CameraPreview.swift` were: the device observers,
14	/// the pending mark, the rebuild it applies, the selection rule and the
15	/// microphone list.
16	///
17	/// **The observers** are `AVCaptureDevice`'s connected and disconnected
18	/// notifications for any device, on main. `show()` adds the pair (one at
19	/// most) and adding it marks the lists pending, so a change made while the
20	/// panel was closed is caught up; `panelWillClose` removes them. A panel
21	/// ordered out for a recording keeps them.
22	///
23	/// **Pending until idle.** A notification marks the lists pending and steps
24	/// the preview (`syncCameraPreview`), whose FIRST act is
25	/// `applyPendingDevices`: it applies only while the panel's phase and the
26	/// recorder are both idle, so a change during a countdown, a recording or a
27	/// landing waits for the first step that finds both idle — the return to
28	/// idle draws the phase, which steps. It never steps the preview itself (no
29	/// recursion) and never persists.
30	///
31	/// **The rebuild** compares each popup's rows (id, title) with the devices
32	/// connected now and rebuilds only a popup that differs, so a menu the
33	/// person has open is not rebuilt for an unrelated device. The selection is
34	/// `hotPlugSelection` over the id held BEFORE the rebuild; the camera is
35	/// selected again — which rebuilds the Format popup, the stored format else
36	/// Best (CAM-6 (2)) — only when its popup was rebuilt or the id changed.
37	/// **No key is written**, so a camera that goes and comes back is selected
38	/// again with its stored format; the next control change writes what the
39	/// popups then show (CAM-5 (2)).
40	extension RecorderPanelController {
41	
42	    /// CAM-8 (3): `stored` when `listed` holds it, else `current` when
43	    /// listed, else nil (the default). `""` counts as nil for both.
44	    static func hotPlugSelection(listed: [String], stored: String?, current: String?) -> String? {
45	        let stored = stored.flatMap { $0.isEmpty ? nil : $0 }
46	        let current = current.flatMap { $0.isEmpty ? nil : $0 }
47	        if let stored, listed.contains(stored) { return stored }
48	        if let current, listed.contains(current) { return current }
49	        return nil
50	    }
51	
52	    /// The microphones connected now: the discovery session
53	    /// `ScreenRecorder.microphone(withID:)` asks, keeping only those whose
54	    /// `isConnected` is true (CAM-8 (5)).
55	    static func connectedMicrophones() -> [AVCaptureDevice] {
56	        AVCaptureDevice.DiscoverySession(
57	            deviceTypes: [.microphone, .external], mediaType: .audio, position: .unspecified
58	        ).devices.filter(\.isConnected)
59	    }
60	
61	    /// `popup`'s rows as a hot-plug compares them.
62	    static func hotPlugRows(of popup: NSPopUpButton) -> [HotPlugRow] {
63	        popup.itemArray.map { HotPlugRow(id: $0.representedObject as? String, title: $0.title) }
64	    }
65	
66	    // MARK: - The observers
67	
68	    /// Idempotent: one pair at most. Adding the pair marks the lists
69	    /// pending, so the sync that follows catches up a change made while the
70	    /// panel was closed.
71	    func observeDevices() {
72	        guard deviceObservers.isEmpty else { return }
73	        let center = NotificationCenter.default
74	        let names = [AVCaptureDevice.wasConnectedNotification, AVCaptureDevice.wasDisconnectedNotification]
75	        for name in names {
76	            let observer = center.addObserver(forName: name, object: nil, queue: .main) {
77	                [weak self] _ in
78	                self?.devicesDidChange()
79	            }
80	            deviceObservers.append(observer)
81	        }
82	        devicesPending = true
83	    }
84	
85	    /// Removes both observers.
86	    func stopObservingDevices() {
87	        deviceObservers.forEach(NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver)
88	        deviceObservers = []
89	    }
90	
91	    /// A device came or went: the lists are pending, and the preview's step
92	    /// applies them first when the panel and the recorder are idle.
93	    func devicesDidChange() {
94	        devicesPending = true
95	        syncCameraPreview()
96	    }
97	
98	    // MARK: - The rebuild
99	
100	    /// CAM-8 (2)–(4): nothing unless pending and both idle; then each popup
101	    /// rebuilt only when its rows differ from the devices connected now, the
102	    /// selection `hotPlugSelection`'s, and the size note refreshed. Writes
103	    /// no key and never steps the preview.
104	    func applyPendingDevices() {
105	        guard devicesPending else { return }
106	        guard phase == .idle, recorder.state == .idle else { return }
107	        devicesPending = false
108	        let defaults = UserDefaults.standard
109	
110	        let cameras = CameraDevices.connected()
111	        let cameraRows =
112	            cameras.isEmpty
113	            ? [HotPlugRow(id: nil, title: Self.noCameraTitle)]
114	            : cameras.map {
115	                HotPlugRow(id: $0.uniqueID, title: CameraDevices.popupTitle(CameraDevices.facts(of: $0)))
116	            }
117	        let currentCamera = selectedCameraID
118	        let cameraRebuilt = Self.hotPlugRows(of: cameraPopup) != cameraRows
119	        if cameraRebuilt { rebuildCameras() }
120	        let camera = Self.hotPlugSelection(
121	            listed: cameras.map(\.uniqueID), stored: defaults.string(forKey: Self.cameraKey),
122	            current: currentCamera)
123	        if cameraRebuilt || camera != selectedCameraID { selectCamera(camera) }
124	
125	        let microphones = Self.connectedMicrophones()
126	        let microphoneRows =
127	            [HotPlugRow(id: nil, title: "Off")]
128	            + microphones.map { HotPlugRow(id: $0.uniqueID, title: $0.localizedName) }
129	        let currentMicrophone = microphonePopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String
130	        if Self.hotPlugRows(of: microphonePopup) != microphoneRows { rebuildMicrophones() }
131	        selectMicrophone(
132	            Self.hotPlugSelection(
133	                listed: microphones.map(\.uniqueID),
134	                stored: defaults.string(forKey: Self.microphoneKey), current: currentMicrophone))
135	        // AU-69 (a): the Enhance box follows a microphone that came or went.
136	        enhanceMicrophoneCheckbox.isEnabled = currentChoice().microphone != nil
137	        refreshSizeNote()
138	    }
139	}

11	// `addMedia`, `view`, `clip(_:in:scope:)` and `trimmed` are internal in
12	// the base file for this one, and `placeBackToBack`, `placeClip`,
13	// `mediaEntry`, `tooShortNote` and `milliseconds` in `+Placing`, because

18	import AppKit
19	
20	extension RecordingLanding {
21	    /// The new back track every microphone clip lands on — ONE track for the
22	    /// whole recording, added once, before the first voice that takes a
23	    /// frame, so a paused recording's voices sit in a row under its pictures
24	    /// as its pictures do, and a recording none of whose voices can be
25	    /// placed adds no empty track.
26	    static let microphoneTrackName = "Microphone"
27	
28	    /// Every stretch's microphone (`voices(of:)`, one per segment and per
29	    /// left-out voice): each file's `add_media` in order, then — when
30	    /// `pictureStarts` is given, one per voice — ONE new back track and each
31	    /// voice's clip by the floor rule, in the same order. A nil
32	    /// `pictureStarts` is `place: false`: the media land and no clip does,
33	    /// R1's rule; a nil ENTRY lands that voice as media only. Answers one
34	    /// media id and one clip id PER VOICE, nil where it has no file, or
35	    /// where it minted no clip — too short for a frame, or wholly under the
36	    /// previous voice, each with its sentence in `notes`.
37	    ///
38	    /// **The floor.** Segment `k`'s voice belongs at `pictureStart_k −
39	    /// micOffset_k`, and with one voice that is R1's rule exactly, floored at
40	    /// 0. With several, two voices on one track can neither overlap — a
41	    /// refusal, or worse a sub-frame overlap the rule ACCEPTS as a
42	    /// transition, minting a cross dissolve between two halves of one
43	    /// recording — nor be placed late (the same wrong sound as R1's negative
44	    /// start put at 0), so the floor for voice `k` is the previous voice's
45	    /// END, and a start below it is head-trimmed to it by the same dance.
46	    /// The floor is READ off the trial, never computed: the previous clip's
47	    /// end is on the frame grid because the core snapped its start and its
48	    /// length, and a sum over descriptor durations would not be. (At an
49	    /// inexact rate even that end is not a grid point, and `placeClip` steps
50	    /// the add up a frame when the core snaps under it.)
51	    ///
52	    /// The track is added on the attempt of the FIRST voice that takes a
53	    /// frame, and kept only when that voice lands: a voice that mints no
54	    /// clip discards its attempt whole, so a recording with no placeable
55	    /// voice adds no empty track. Its id is `next_id` off the trial at that
56	    /// moment, unchanged by a discarded attempt.
57	    static func addMicrophones(
58	        _ voices: [Voice], pictureStarts: [Ticks?]?, scope: UInt32?,
59	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
60	    ) throws -> (media: [UInt32?], clips: [UInt32?]) {
61	        precondition(
62	            pictureStarts.map { $0.count == voices.count } ?? true,
63	            "one picture start per voice")
64	        var media: [UInt32?] = []
65	        for voice in voices {
66	            if let mic = voice.descriptor {
67	                media.append(try addMedia(mic, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
68	            } else {
69	                media.append(nil)
70	            }
71	        }
72	        let none: [UInt32?] = voices.map { _ in nil }
73	        guard let starts = pictureStarts else { return (media, none) }
74	        var track: UInt32?
75	        var clips: [UInt32?] = []
76	        var floor: Ticks = 0
77	        for (k, voice) in voices.enumerated() {
78	            guard let id = media[k], let start = starts[k] else {
79	                clips.append(nil)
80	                continue
81	            }
82	            var attempt = trial
83	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
84	            let on: UInt32
85	            if let added = track {
86	                on = added
87	            } else {
88	                on = attempt.snapshot.nextId
89	                let addTrack = ReelOp.addTrack(index: 0, name: microphoneTrackName)
90	                guard let withTrack = try attempt.applying(addTrack.scoped(scope)).project
91	                else {
92	                    throw ReelCoreError(message: "A track for the microphone could not be added.")
93	                }
94	                attempt = withTrack
95	                attemptOps.append(addTrack)
96	            }
97	            guard
98	                let placed = try addMicrophoneClip(
99	                    id, on: on, pictureAt: start, offset: voice.offset, floor: floor,
100	                    scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps, notes: &notes)
101	            else {
102	                clips.append(nil)
103	                continue
104	            }
105	            trial = attempt
106	            ops += attemptOps
107	            track = on
108	            clips.append(placed.id)
109	            floor = placed.end
110	        }
111	        return (media, clips)
112	    }
113	
114	    /// One voice's clip on `track`, at `pictureAt − offset` and never below
115	    /// `floor` — 0 for the first voice, the previous voice's end after it.
116	    /// nil, with a sentence in `notes`, for a voice that gets no clip; the
117	    /// trial and the ops are advanced only for a clip returned.
118	    ///
119	    /// **The sign.** `offset` is the screen's did-start minus the
120	    /// microphone's, in ticks; positive means the picture began AFTER the
121	    /// microphone, so the microphone's content LEADS and its clip starts
122	    /// that much earlier than the picture's. R0 measured it centred near
123	    /// zero with a 35 ms scatter (road map 3, R0 q6b) and a different number
124	    /// at every resume (q7), and the landing applies each segment's measured
125	    /// number — never a constant, never the first segment's.
126	    ///
127	    /// **When that start is below the floor** — the picture at 0 with the
128	    /// microphone ahead of it, or a later voice whose picture began less
129	    /// than its offset after the previous voice ended — the clip cannot
130	    /// start there: below 0 there is no timeline, below the previous voice's
131	    /// end there is a clip, and placing it AT the floor would leave the
132	    /// voice LATE by the difference. So the head is trimmed off instead, and
133	    /// it stays one grouped edit: `add_clip` at the floor, `trim_start` to
134	    /// the landed start + head (the core sets the start there and advances
135	    /// `in` by the same amount — `core/src/edit_clip.rs`), `move_clip` back
136	    /// by what the trim advanced, read off the trimmed clip (the head, at
137	    /// an exact rate; at an inexact one the grid point nearest it). A
138	    /// `slip` would be the one-op spelling and cannot be used: the clip
139	    /// covers its whole media, so the slip's clamp reduces it to nothing.
140	    /// The head is the core's own snap of the shortfall
141	    /// (`ReelTime.snapToFrame`, the rounding every time argument gets), so a
142	    /// start within half a frame of the floor makes no trim and the two ops
143	    /// are not sent — the core's snap of that start lands it on the floor —
144	    /// while a start further below is trimmed rather than left to the snap,
145	    /// because the core would snap it to the frame BELOW the floor: at 0
146	    /// clamped up and late by a frame, above 0 a one-frame overlap the rule
147	    /// accepts as a transition. Limit: the grid is the picture's frame — at
148	    /// 60 fps 16.7 ms — so the alignment is exact to half a frame and no
149	    /// finer.
150	    ///
151	    /// **Every step is read back, and two things are decided by what comes
152	    /// back** (the R2 review). `trim_start` clamps its `to` at a frame
153	    /// before the clip's end, so a voice no longer than its head — an 80 ms
154	    /// file whose picture began 100 ms after it — used to be trimmed to a
155	    /// one-frame sliver and then moved back INTO the previous voice, which
156	    /// `move_clips` refused: `applying(_ ops:)` still answered non-nil (the
157	    /// add and the trim had changed something), the trial "succeeded", and
158	    /// the commit ran a refused op inside its undo step with the sliver
159	    /// sitting late. Now the trimmed clip's start is compared with the
160	    /// core's own snap of the requested `to`, and a start that is not it is
161	    /// the clamp: the voice is wholly under its head, mints NO clip, and its
162	    /// sentence names the file. And the moved clip must land exactly where
163	    /// the core's snap of the delta says, at or above the floor, or the
164	    /// throw names the file — a refused op can never ride a committed list.
165	    /// At an INEXACT rate the move's landing can be a tick under a floor
166	    /// that is a grid point (the delta and the trim round separately; grid
167	    /// points are not closed under addition), which the rule would accept
168	    /// and dress as a transition, so that one case is done once more a
169	    /// frame up with a frame more head: the content stays aligned to the
170	    /// tick, the voice starts a sub-frame gap after the previous one, and
171	    /// its first frame past the head is the price — the documented limit of
172	    /// such a rate, beside the pictures' own sub-frame gap.
173	    static func addMicrophoneClip(
174	        _ media: UInt32, on track: UInt32, pictureAt: Ticks, offset: Ticks, floor: Ticks,
175	        scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
176	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
177	        let file = try mediaEntry(media, in: trial, scope: scope)
178	        let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
179	        if let note = tooShortNote(file, at: fps) {
180	            notes.append(note)
181	            return nil
182	        }
183	        let start = pictureAt - offset
184	        let head = start < floor ? ReelTime.snapToFrame(floor - start, fps: fps) : 0
185	        guard head > 0 else {
186	            guard
187	                let placed = try placeClip(
188	                    media, on: track, at: max(start, floor), notBelow: floor, scope: scope,
189	                    to: &trial, ops: &ops)
190	            else {
191	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(file.path) could not be placed on its track.")
192	            }
193	            return placed
194	        }
195	        let frame = fps.frameDuration
196	        for (at, head) in [(floor, head), (floor + frame, head + frame)] {
197	            var attempt = trial
198	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
199	            guard
200	                let placed = try headTrimmed(
201	                    media, file: file, on: track, at: at, head: head, floor: floor, fps: fps,
202	                    scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps)
203	            else {
204	                notes.append(underNote(file, head: head, floor: floor))
205	                return nil
206	            }
207	            if placed.start >= floor {
208	                trial = attempt
209	                ops += attemptOps
210	                return placed
211	            }
212	        }
213	        throw ReelCoreError(
214	            message: "\(file.path) could not be placed clear of the previous microphone clip.")
215	    }
216	
217	    /// The dance once, on `trial`: the add at `at` (never under `floor`),
218	    /// the trim to the landed start + `head`, the move back by what the trim
219	    /// advanced. nil when the trim clamped — the voice is wholly under its
220	    /// head — with the trial left as it was; every other surprise is a
221	    /// throw naming the file. The clip returned may still sit a tick under
222	    /// the floor at an inexact rate, which the caller reads.
223	    static func headTrimmed(
224	        _ media: UInt32, file: MediaSnapshot, on track: UInt32, at: Ticks, head: Ticks,
225	        floor: Ticks, fps: Fps, scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
226	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
227	        guard
228	            let added = try placeClip(
229	                media, on: track, at: at, notBelow: floor, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
230	        else {
231	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(file.path) could not be placed on its track.")
232	        }
233	        let trim = ReelOp.trimStart(clip: added.id, to: added.start + head)
234	        let promisedTrim = ReelTime.snapToFrame(added.start + head, fps: fps)
235	        guard let trimmed = try trial.applying(trim.scoped(scope)).project,
236	            try clip(added.id, in: trimmed, scope: scope).start == promisedTrim
237	        else { return nil }
238	        let advanced = promisedTrim - added.start
239	        let move = ReelOp.moveClip(clips: [added.id], delta: -advanced)
240	        let promisedStart = promisedTrim + ReelTime.snapToFrame(-advanced, fps: fps)
241	        guard let moved = try trimmed.applying(move.scoped(scope)).project else {
242	            throw ReelCoreError(
243	                message: "\(file.path) could not be moved back by its \(milliseconds(advanced)) ms head.")
244	        }
245	        let landed = try clip(added.id, in: moved, scope: scope)
246	        guard landed.start == promisedStart, landed.source.sourceIn == advanced else {
247	            throw ReelCoreError(
248	                message: "\(file.path) landed at \(landed.start) with \(landed.source.sourceIn) "
249	                    + "trimmed, not at \(promisedStart) with \(advanced).")
250	        }
251	        trial = moved
252	        ops += [trim, move]
253	        return landed
254	    }
255	
256	    /// The sentence for a voice wholly under its head.
257	    private static func underNote(_ file: MediaSnapshot, head: Ticks, floor: Ticks) -> String {
258	        let clear = floor == 0 ? "the start of the timeline" : "the previous microphone clip"
259	        return "\(file.path) was added to the media list without a clip: less than a frame of "
260	            + "it would remain after the \(milliseconds(head)) ms head that keeps it clear of "
261	            + "\(clear)."
262	    }
263	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c));
  `PlanSegment.path` (the clip alone when absent) and `origin` (nil) read a nested audio
  segment's instance (spec §11 TX-10); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113); `PlanGate` and
  `gates` a gated clip's hide-while-silent gate (format 43, spec §11 CO-93). `AudioProps.swift`
  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map
  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,
  `hideIdleSteps` and `polished`,
  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and
  `RecipeCursor` (the recipe layer's `cursor`, `media` and `at` required).
  `CutoutProps.swift` (format 39, road map creator-jobs CO2a1, spec §11 CO-20, CO-21;
  `foreground` and the image arm format 41, CO10a, CO-100, CO-101) holds `CutoutSubject`
  (`person`, `foreground`), `CutoutQuality`, `CutoutBackground`, `CutoutProps` (`VideoProps.cutout` and
  `VideoPatch.cutout`; its `dictionary` writes all five keys), `CutoutPatch` (the sparse
  write `VideoPatch.cutoutPart` carries — written under `cutout` only when `cutout` is nil,
  never decoded — so a Background, Edge or Feather row writes its own key alone, CO3),
  `RecipeCutoutMaskKind` (`media`, and `image`, drawn since CO10b from the
  picture's one mask, CO-107),
  `RecipeCutoutMask` (`kind` and `media` required; `subject` lenient,
  `person` when absent, CO-101) and `RecipeCutout` (the recipe layer's
  `cutout`, `mask` required; `subjectCopy`, CO-51); `RecipeLayer.videoProps` passes no cutout — the recipe's is a draw
  instruction, not the clip's props. `VideoProps.swift` (`VideoProps`),
  `ClipSnapshot.swift` (`ClipSource` with its nested `CodingKeys`, `ClipSnapshot`,
  `TransitionSnapshot`) and `TrackSnapshot.swift` (`TrackSnapshot`) are pure moves out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T11–T13). `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

  `AVPlayerLayer.videoRect`, which is the aspect of the BUFFER — the reason

  the render's font, kern and paragraph style, the editor's own ink.

  editor's keys (spec §11 K-2): bare Return applies, a modified Return is a
  newline, Esc over changed text asks Cancel · Revert · Apply in a sheet
  whose Apply goes through `performGroupedEdit` (a sheet completion is
  outside an AppKit event). Its `textCommitOp` is the one op both canvas
  commits send (Return or blur, and the sheet's Apply), through
  `TextPatch.contentEdit`, so a timed page whose count changes lands

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**

  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a

  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2

  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's

  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,

  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the

  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an

  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.

  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.

  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`

  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map
  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),

  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,

  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.
