1	// app/Sources/RecordingLanding+Microphone.swift — the microphone half of
2	// the landing (road map 3, R1b; per segment since R2b), a PURE MOVE out of
3	// `RecordingLanding.swift` landed alone at the 400-line cap (R2's toll) and
4	// then grown here: the name the microphone's track carries,
5	// `addMicrophones` (every stretch's voice on ONE back track,
6	// by the floor rule — a left-out segment's readable voice, #181 item 2,
7	// among them, its stretches in `+LeftOut`) and `addMicrophoneClip`, the
8	// head-trim dance with every step of it READ BACK. `remainderPlacement`
9	// (everything a fresh untitled document does not already hold) and the two
10	// undo steps' names are `+Remainder`'s since camera-recording CR3-0.
11	// `addMedia`, `view`, `clip(_:in:scope:)` and `trimmed` are internal in
12	// the base file for this one, and `placeBackToBack`, `placeClip`,
13	// `mediaEntry`, `tooShortNote` and `milliseconds` in `+Placing`, because
14	// `private` does not cross a file. `headTrimmed` is internal for the same
15	// reason since camera-recording CR3b: `+Camera`'s clips take the same dance
16	// (spec §11 CAM-10 (2)).
17	
18	import AppKit
19	
20	extension RecordingLanding {
21	    /// The new back track every microphone clip lands on — ONE track for the
22	    /// whole recording, added once, before the first voice that takes a
23	    /// frame, so a paused recording's voices sit in a row under its pictures
24	    /// as its pictures do, and a recording none of whose voices can be
25	    /// placed adds no empty track.
26	    static let microphoneTrackName = "Microphone"
27	
28	    /// Every stretch's microphone (`voices(of:)`, one per segment and per
29	    /// left-out voice): each file's `add_media` in order, then — when
30	    /// `pictureStarts` is given, one per voice — ONE new back track and each
31	    /// voice's clip by the floor rule, in the same order. A nil
32	    /// `pictureStarts` is `place: false`: the media land and no clip does,
33	    /// R1's rule; a nil ENTRY lands that voice as media only. Answers one
34	    /// media id and one clip id PER VOICE, nil where it has no file, or
35	    /// where it minted no clip — too short for a frame, or wholly under the
36	    /// previous voice, each with its sentence in `notes`.
37	    ///
38	    /// **The floor.** Segment `k`'s voice belongs at `pictureStart_k −
39	    /// micOffset_k`, and with one voice that is R1's rule exactly, floored at
40	    /// 0. With several, two voices on one track can neither overlap — a
41	    /// refusal, or worse a sub-frame overlap the rule ACCEPTS as a
42	    /// transition, minting a cross dissolve between two halves of one
43	    /// recording — nor be placed late (the same wrong sound as R1's negative
44	    /// start put at 0), so the floor for voice `k` is the previous voice's
45	    /// END, and a start below it is head-trimmed to it by the same dance.
46	    /// The floor is READ off the trial, never computed: the previous clip's
47	    /// end is on the frame grid because the core snapped its start and its
48	    /// length, and a sum over descriptor durations would not be. (At an
49	    /// inexact rate even that end is not a grid point, and `placeClip` steps
50	    /// the add up a frame when the core snaps under it.)
51	    ///
52	    /// The track is added on the attempt of the FIRST voice that takes a
53	    /// frame, and kept only when that voice lands: a voice that mints no
54	    /// clip discards its attempt whole, so a recording with no placeable
55	    /// voice adds no empty track. Its id is `next_id` off the trial at that
56	    /// moment, unchanged by a discarded attempt.
57	    static func addMicrophones(
58	        _ voices: [Voice], pictureStarts: [Ticks?]?, scope: UInt32?,
59	        to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
60	    ) throws -> (media: [UInt32?], clips: [UInt32?]) {
61	        precondition(
62	            pictureStarts.map { $0.count == voices.count } ?? true,
63	            "one picture start per voice")
64	        var media: [UInt32?] = []
65	        for voice in voices {
66	            if let mic = voice.descriptor {
67	                media.append(try addMedia(mic, to: &trial, ops: &ops))
68	            } else {
69	                media.append(nil)
70	            }
71	        }
72	        let none: [UInt32?] = voices.map { _ in nil }
73	        guard let starts = pictureStarts else { return (media, none) }
74	        var track: UInt32?
75	        var clips: [UInt32?] = []
76	        var floor: Ticks = 0
77	        for (k, voice) in voices.enumerated() {
78	            guard let id = media[k], let start = starts[k] else {
79	                clips.append(nil)
80	                continue
81	            }
82	            var attempt = trial
83	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
84	            let on: UInt32
85	            if let added = track {
86	                on = added
87	            } else {
88	                on = attempt.snapshot.nextId
89	                let addTrack = ReelOp.addTrack(index: 0, name: microphoneTrackName)
90	                guard let withTrack = try attempt.applying(addTrack.scoped(scope)).project
91	                else {
92	                    throw ReelCoreError(message: "A track for the microphone could not be added.")
93	                }
94	                attempt = withTrack
95	                attemptOps.append(addTrack)
96	            }
97	            guard
98	                let placed = try addMicrophoneClip(
99	                    id, on: on, pictureAt: start, offset: voice.offset, floor: floor,
100	                    scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps, notes: &notes)
101	            else {
102	                clips.append(nil)
103	                continue
104	            }
105	            trial = attempt
106	            ops += attemptOps
107	            track = on
108	            clips.append(placed.id)
109	            floor = placed.end
110	        }
111	        return (media, clips)
112	    }
113	
114	    /// One voice's clip on `track`, at `pictureAt − offset` and never below
115	    /// `floor` — 0 for the first voice, the previous voice's end after it.
116	    /// nil, with a sentence in `notes`, for a voice that gets no clip; the
117	    /// trial and the ops are advanced only for a clip returned.
118	    ///
119	    /// **The sign.** `offset` is the screen's did-start minus the
120	    /// microphone's, in ticks; positive means the picture began AFTER the
121	    /// microphone, so the microphone's content LEADS and its clip starts
122	    /// that much earlier than the picture's. R0 measured it centred near
123	    /// zero with a 35 ms scatter (road map 3, R0 q6b) and a different number
124	    /// at every resume (q7), and the landing applies each segment's measured
125	    /// number — never a constant, never the first segment's.
126	    ///
127	    /// **When that start is below the floor** — the picture at 0 with the
128	    /// microphone ahead of it, or a later voice whose picture began less
129	    /// than its offset after the previous voice ended — the clip cannot
130	    /// start there: below 0 there is no timeline, below the previous voice's
131	    /// end there is a clip, and placing it AT the floor would leave the
132	    /// voice LATE by the difference. So the head is trimmed off instead, and
133	    /// it stays one grouped edit: `add_clip` at the floor, `trim_start` to
134	    /// the landed start + head (the core sets the start there and advances
135	    /// `in` by the same amount — `core/src/edit_clip.rs`), `move_clip` back
136	    /// by what the trim advanced, read off the trimmed clip (the head, at
137	    /// an exact rate; at an inexact one the grid point nearest it). A
138	    /// `slip` would be the one-op spelling and cannot be used: the clip
139	    /// covers its whole media, so the slip's clamp reduces it to nothing.
140	    /// The head is the core's own snap of the shortfall
141	    /// (`ReelTime.snapToFrame`, the rounding every time argument gets), so a
142	    /// start within half a frame of the floor makes no trim and the two ops
143	    /// are not sent — the core's snap of that start lands it on the floor —
144	    /// while a start further below is trimmed rather than left to the snap,
145	    /// because the core would snap it to the frame BELOW the floor: at 0
146	    /// clamped up and late by a frame, above 0 a one-frame overlap the rule
147	    /// accepts as a transition. Limit: the grid is the picture's frame — at
148	    /// 60 fps 16.7 ms — so the alignment is exact to half a frame and no
149	    /// finer.
150	    ///
151	    /// **Every step is read back, and two things are decided by what comes
152	    /// back** (the R2 review). `trim_start` clamps its `to` at a frame
153	    /// before the clip's end, so a voice no longer than its head — an 80 ms
154	    /// file whose picture began 100 ms after it — used to be trimmed to a
155	    /// one-frame sliver and then moved back INTO the previous voice, which
156	    /// `move_clips` refused: `applying(_ ops:)` still answered non-nil (the
157	    /// add and the trim had changed something), the trial "succeeded", and
158	    /// the commit ran a refused op inside its undo step with the sliver
159	    /// sitting late. Now the trimmed clip's start is compared with the
160	    /// core's own snap of the requested `to`, and a start that is not it is
161	    /// the clamp: the voice is wholly under its head, mints NO clip, and its
162	    /// sentence names the file. And the moved clip must land exactly where
163	    /// the core's snap of the delta says, at or above the floor, or the
164	    /// throw names the file — a refused op can never ride a committed list.
165	    /// At an INEXACT rate the move's landing can be a tick under a floor
166	    /// that is a grid point (the delta and the trim round separately; grid
167	    /// points are not closed under addition), which the rule would accept
168	    /// and dress as a transition, so that one case is done once more a
169	    /// frame up with a frame more head: the content stays aligned to the
170	    /// tick, the voice starts a sub-frame gap after the previous one, and
171	    /// its first frame past the head is the price — the documented limit of
172	    /// such a rate, beside the pictures' own sub-frame gap.
173	    static func addMicrophoneClip(
174	        _ media: UInt32, on track: UInt32, pictureAt: Ticks, offset: Ticks, floor: Ticks,
175	        scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp], notes: inout [String]
176	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
177	        let file = try mediaEntry(media, in: trial, scope: scope)
178	        let fps = try view(of: trial, scope: scope).snapshot.canvas.fps
179	        if let note = tooShortNote(file, at: fps) {
180	            notes.append(note)
181	            return nil
182	        }
183	        let start = pictureAt - offset
184	        let head = start < floor ? ReelTime.snapToFrame(floor - start, fps: fps) : 0
185	        guard head > 0 else {
186	            guard
187	                let placed = try placeClip(
188	                    media, on: track, at: max(start, floor), notBelow: floor, scope: scope,
189	                    to: &trial, ops: &ops)
190	            else {
191	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(file.path) could not be placed on its track.")
192	            }
193	            return placed
194	        }
195	        let frame = fps.frameDuration
196	        for (at, head) in [(floor, head), (floor + frame, head + frame)] {
197	            var attempt = trial
198	            var attemptOps: [ReelOp] = []
199	            guard
200	                let placed = try headTrimmed(
201	                    media, file: file, on: track, at: at, head: head, floor: floor, fps: fps,
202	                    scope: scope, to: &attempt, ops: &attemptOps)
203	            else {
204	                notes.append(underNote(file, head: head, floor: floor))
205	                return nil
206	            }
207	            if placed.start >= floor {
208	                trial = attempt
209	                ops += attemptOps
210	                return placed
211	            }
212	        }
213	        throw ReelCoreError(
214	            message: "\(file.path) could not be placed clear of the previous microphone clip.")
215	    }
216	
217	    /// The dance once, on `trial`: the add at `at` (never under `floor`),
218	    /// the trim to the landed start + `head`, the move back by what the trim
219	    /// advanced. nil when the trim clamped — the voice is wholly under its
220	    /// head — with the trial left as it was; every other surprise is a
221	    /// throw naming the file. The clip returned may still sit a tick under
222	    /// the floor at an inexact rate, which the caller reads.
223	    static func headTrimmed(
224	        _ media: UInt32, file: MediaSnapshot, on track: UInt32, at: Ticks, head: Ticks,
225	        floor: Ticks, fps: Fps, scope: UInt32?, to trial: inout ReelProject, ops: inout [ReelOp]
226	    ) throws -> ClipSnapshot? {
227	        guard
228	            let added = try placeClip(
229	                media, on: track, at: at, notBelow: floor, scope: scope, to: &trial, ops: &ops)
230	        else {
231	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(file.path) could not be placed on its track.")
232	        }
233	        let trim = ReelOp.trimStart(clip: added.id, to: added.start + head)
234	        let promisedTrim = ReelTime.snapToFrame(added.start + head, fps: fps)
235	        guard let trimmed = try trial.applying(trim.scoped(scope)).project,
236	            try clip(added.id, in: trimmed, scope: scope).start == promisedTrim
237	        else { return nil }
238	        let advanced = promisedTrim - added.start
239	        let move = ReelOp.moveClip(clips: [added.id], delta: -advanced)
240	        let promisedStart = promisedTrim + ReelTime.snapToFrame(-advanced, fps: fps)
241	        guard let moved = try trimmed.applying(move.scoped(scope)).project else {
242	            throw ReelCoreError(
243	                message: "\(file.path) could not be moved back by its \(milliseconds(advanced)) ms head.")
244	        }
245	        let landed = try clip(added.id, in: moved, scope: scope)
246	        guard landed.start == promisedStart, landed.source.sourceIn == advanced else {
247	            throw ReelCoreError(
248	                message: "\(file.path) landed at \(landed.start) with \(landed.source.sourceIn) "
249	                    + "trimmed, not at \(promisedStart) with \(advanced).")
250	        }
251	        trial = moved
252	        ops += [trim, move]
253	        return landed
254	    }
255	
256	    /// The sentence for a voice wholly under its head.
257	    private static func underNote(_ file: MediaSnapshot, head: Ticks, floor: Ticks) -> String {
258	        let clear = floor == 0 ? "the start of the timeline" : "the previous microphone clip"
259	        return "\(file.path) was added to the media list without a clip: less than a frame of "
260	            + "it would remain after the \(milliseconds(head)) ms head that keeps it clear of "
261	            + "\(clear)."
262	    }
263	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

input.content:
---
title: "Record a camera beside the screen"
description: "Record your camera at the same time as a display or a window, for a talking head over a screencast, and choose how it lands."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Tick one box and Frame Job records your camera at the same time as the screen, for a talking head over a screencast. The camera lands as an ordinary clip on a track of its own, already laid out over the screen.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Record the camera too', 'New Recording panel ▸ Layout', "New Recording panel ▸ Remove the camera's background when it lands"]}
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The Screen Recording and Camera permissions, and the Microphone permission when you choose a microphone."
/>

## Record the screen and the camera

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ New Recording…**, and set **Source** to a display or **Window…**.

2. Tick **Record the camera too**. **Camera**, **Format**, **Layout** and **Remove the camera's background when it lands** go live, and a **Preview** of the camera appears under **Format**.

3. Choose the camera in **Camera**, and its size and frame rate in **Format**. [Record a camera](/recording/record-a-camera/) explains both lists.

4. Choose a [layout](#choose-a-layout).

5. Choose a **Microphone** if you want your voice. The camera's movie has no sound of its own.

6. Press **Record**. Frame Job checks its permissions, then counts down from 3.

7. The panel leaves the screen. Pause and stop from the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or the **File** menu.

</Steps>

**Record the camera too** is off until you tick it, and Frame Job remembers it between launches. It's live only with a display or **Window…** as the source. **Camera** and **Microphone Only** grey it out, keeping its value.

**System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows** and **Rate** stay live and apply to the screen, and the note under **Size** describes the screen. The camera records at the frame rate of its **Format**.

### What Record checks

Pressing **Record** stops at the first thing missing, in this order:

1. A camera. With none connected, the panel says "No camera is connected."
2. The Screen Recording permission.
3. The Input Monitoring permission, only with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) ticked.
4. The Camera permission.
5. The Microphone permission, only with a microphone chosen.

[Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/) says what each one asks of you.

### The preview

The camera starts as soon as you tick the box, so it has settled at its frame rate by the time recording begins. Unticking the box, choosing **Microphone Only** or closing the panel turns it off.

The preview shows the chosen camera at the chosen format. When it can't, it says why:

| The preview says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "No camera is connected." | There's no camera to show. |
| "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera." | You haven't allowed the Camera permission yet. Showing the panel never asks for it. Pressing **Record** does. |
| "The camera is recording." | An agent is recording a camera right now. The picture comes back when it ends. |
| Another sentence | The reason the camera couldn't start. Untick and tick the box, or reopen the panel, to try again. |

## Choose a layout

**Layout** sets how the camera sits with the screen when the recording lands.

| Layout | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Corner** | The default. The camera sits in the bottom-right corner, scaled to fit a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % guide of [**View ▸ Safe Areas**](/canvas/safe-areas/). |
| **Rounded Corner** | The same corner with rounded edges. |
| **Circle** | The same corner as a circle. |
| **Side by Side** | The screen and the camera next to each other. |
| **Camera Full** | The camera fills the canvas. |

When the recording lands, each stretch's camera movie goes on one new track named **Camera**, in front of everything, lined up with that stretch's screen clip. A recording you never paused has one stretch. A paused one has [several](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches).

| --- | --- |
| An open project | **Add Recording**, for the screen, the camera and any microphone |
| A new project, one stretch | **Add Camera**, or **Add Camera and Microphone** with a microphone. The screen movie is the project itself. |
| A new project, several stretches | **Add Recording Segments** |

The layout starts at the camera clip's first frame, so the screen keeps its full picture until the camera arrives. It ends with that stretch's screen clip or its camera clip, whichever is later.

---
title: "Record a voice-over"
description: "Record narration from your microphone with no picture, at the playhead of the project you're editing or as a new project."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A voice-over is the microphone alone, with no picture. Use it to record narration over your edit: it lands at the playhead, on a new track of its own.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ Source ▸ Microphone Only"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The Microphone permission. Screen Recording isn't needed."
/>

## Record a voice-over

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to where the narration should start.

2. Choose **File ▸ New Recording…**, and set **Source** to **Microphone Only**.

3. Choose your microphone in **Microphone**.

4. Check **Record Into**: the project to land in, or **New Project**.

5. Press **Record**. Frame Job checks the Microphone permission, then counts down from 3.

6. Speak. The panel stays up while you do.

7. Press **Stop**. The button reads **Stopping…** and then **Adding…**, and the voice-over lands. The panel stays up, back on **Record**, ready for another take.

</Steps>

With **Microphone** set to **Off**, **Record** starts nothing and the panel says "Microphone Only records the microphone alone — choose a microphone first."

The controls that only make sense for a picture grey out, keeping their values for next time: **System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows**, **Cursor** and **Record shortcuts**. The note under **Size** reads "no picture — the microphone alone". **Rate** stays live, because it sets the frame rate of a new project.

Frame Job keeps **Microphone Only** in **Source** until you quit, then goes back to your display.

## While it records

Nothing on screen is being filmed, so the panel stays up:

- Its rows are locked.
- The [level meter](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/#check-your-level) stays live.
- The footnote at the bottom left shows ● and the elapsed time, or ❚❚ and the time held still while paused.
- **Record** reads **Stop**, and a **Pause** button stands beside it, reading **Resume** while paused.

The countdown and the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) work as they do for a screen recording, so you can also pause and stop from the menu bar, or from **File ▸ Pause Recording** and **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>).

**Close** takes the panel away and the voice-over carries on. To bring the panel back, click **New Recording…** on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/). <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> won't do it, because it stops the recording.

## Where a voice-over lands

**In an open project,** each [stretch](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches) between pauses is its own file, and they land end to end from the playhead on one new back track named **Microphone**. It's all one undo step, **Add Recording**. If a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) is open, they land inside it.

A voice-over always gets a new track. It never goes on an existing one, even one already named **Microphone**.

**As a new project,** the first file is the project itself, audio only at 1920×1080 and the frame rate in **Rate**. Later files follow it on its one track, as one undo step named **Add Recording Segments**.

Either way they're ordinary audio clips, with everything in the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). To clean your voice up as it lands, tick [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/).

## The files

Each stretch is an `.m4a` file in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by the moment it began, for example `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a`. See [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/).

## Good to know

- If the microphone stops on its own, for example because it's unplugged, the voice-over ends there. What was recorded lands, and the note reads "The microphone stopped recording on its own: … The voice-over ends where it stopped."
- A **Resume** that fails shows its reason in the panel's note, and the voice-over stays paused. Try again, or press **Stop** to land what you have.
- A file too short to fill one frame goes to the media list without a clip, and a note says so. If that's every file, no **Microphone** track is added.
- A project already at its track limit can't take the new track. The files stay on disk and the note names them. See [Limits](/reference/limits/).

## With an agent

`record_screen` records a voice-over too. An agent gets your Mac's default microphone rather than a chosen one, and there's no countdown. It can't pass any of the screen settings with a voice-over. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/)
- [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/)
- [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/)
- [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/)

---
title: "System audio and the microphone"
description: "Record what your Mac plays and your voice as two separate sounds, check your level, and see how the microphone lines up with the picture."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A recording can carry two sounds: what your Mac plays, and your voice. Frame Job keeps them apart, so you can set the level of each on its own after the recording lands.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where={['New Recording panel ▸ System Audio', 'New Recording panel ▸ Microphone']}
  tools="record_screen"
  needs={['System Audio: the Screen Recording permission', 'Microphone: the Microphone permission']}
/>

<Shot
  name="16-recorder-panel.panel"
  alt="The New Recording panel. Microphone is set to Off with a level meter beside it, and the System Audio switch below it is on."
/>

## Record what your Mac plays

**System Audio** records the sound from every app but Frame Job, as the movie's own stereo 48 kHz sound track. It's on until you turn it off, and Frame Job remembers your choice.

With it off, the movie has no sound track at all. The switch applies to the screen, so **Camera** and **Microphone Only** in **Source** grey it out, keeping its value.

## Play the timeline while you record

Frame Job's own sound is never recorded, whether or not **Include Frame Job windows** is on. You can play your timeline during a recording and its sound won't be in the file.

## Record your voice

Choose a microphone in **Microphone**. **Off** comes first and is the default, then every connected microphone by name. Frame Job remembers your choice, and falls back to **Off** if that microphone isn't connected.

It works with every source. The voice goes into a second file beside the movie, named after it with ` (Microphone)` added, and never into the movie. With a chosen microphone, pressing **Record** checks the [Microphone permission](/recording/permissions/) first.

To clean your voice up as it lands, tick [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/). To record your voice with no picture, see [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/).

## Check your level

A meter sits beside **Microphone**. It starts moving at the countdown, not when you choose the microphone, so the 3, 2, 1 is your chance to check your level before the recording starts.

It stays live through the recording, and goes silent while paused. For a display or a window the panel leaves the screen once recording begins, so you only see the meter during the countdown. For a camera on its own or a voice-over, the panel stays up and so does the meter.

## Your first words are kept

The microphone starts during the countdown, not when the recording does, so your first words are in the file. A camera's capture starts early the same way. Both are let go if you cancel the countdown, close the panel, or the start fails.

## How the microphone lands

Each file lands on one new back track named **Microphone**, lined up with its picture, so your voice and the computer's sound have separate volumes.

Frame Job measures how far apart the two files started, for each stretch of a [paused recording](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches) separately, and places the clip to match. The alignment is exact to half a frame.

If your voice started before its clip could, at the very start of the timeline or just after the previous microphone clip, the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip being placed late.

If no voice can be placed, no empty track is added. [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) covers the undo steps.

## If the microphone stops

A microphone that fails doesn't stop a screen or camera recording. The picture keeps going, the meter goes silent, and the panel's note reads "The microphone stopped: … The picture is still recording." What the microphone wrote lands with the recording.

A [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/#good-to-know) is different. With nothing else recording, it ends there.

## Plug devices in and take them out

The **Camera**, **Format** and **Microphone** lists follow the devices you plug in or take away.

- Changes apply only while the panel is idle, so nothing moves during a countdown, a recording or a landing. A change that waited applies when the panel goes idle.
- A change made while the panel was closed is picked up when it next shows.
- A microphone you take away falls back to **Off**. A camera falls back to the default camera, or to **None connected** when there's no camera left.
- When a device comes back it's chosen again, and a camera comes back with its stored format.
- Plugging in or removing a device doesn't change what the panel remembers. The next control you change saves whatever the lists show at that moment, so a device that's away at that point is forgotten.
- A list is rebuilt only when its own devices changed, so a menu you have open isn't disturbed by an unrelated device.

## With an agent

An agent turns each sound on or off rather than choosing a device. Its microphone is your Mac's default microphone, off unless it asks. It can't ask for the Microphone permission either: that takes one press of **Record** in the panel. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
- [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/)
- [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/)
- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)

/>

## Record what your Mac plays

**System Audio** records the sound from every app but Frame Job, as the movie's own stereo 48 kHz sound track. It's on until you turn it off, and Frame Job remembers your choice.

With it off, the movie has no sound track at all. The switch applies to the screen, so **Camera** and **Microphone Only** in **Source** grey it out, keeping its value.

## Play the timeline while you record

Frame Job's own sound is never recorded, whether or not **Include Frame Job windows** is on. You can play your timeline during a recording and its sound won't be in the file.

## Record your voice

Choose a microphone in **Microphone**. **Off** comes first and is the default, then every connected microphone by name. Frame Job remembers your choice, and falls back to **Off** if that microphone isn't connected.

It works with every source. The voice goes into a second file beside the movie, named after it with ` (Microphone)` added, and never into the movie. With a chosen microphone, pressing **Record** checks the [Microphone permission](/recording/permissions/) first.

To clean your voice up as it lands, tick [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/). To record your voice with no picture, see [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/).

## Check your level

A meter sits beside **Microphone**. It starts moving at the countdown, not when you choose the microphone, so the 3, 2, 1 is your chance to check your level before the recording starts.

It stays live through the recording, and goes silent while paused. For a display or a window the panel leaves the screen once recording begins, so you only see the meter during the countdown. For a camera on its own or a voice-over, the panel stays up and so does the meter.

## Your first words are kept

The microphone starts during the countdown, not when the recording does, so your first words are in the file. A camera's capture starts early the same way. Both are let go if you cancel the countdown, close the panel, or the start fails.

## How the microphone lands

Each file lands on one new back track named **Microphone**, lined up with its picture, so your voice and the computer's sound have separate volumes.

Frame Job measures how far apart the two files started, for each stretch of a [paused recording](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches) separately, and places the clip to match. The alignment is exact to half a frame.

If your voice started before its clip could, at the very start of the timeline or just after the previous microphone clip, the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip being placed late.

If no voice can be placed, no empty track is added. [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) covers the undo steps.

## If the microphone stops

A microphone that fails doesn't stop a screen or camera recording. The picture keeps going, the meter goes silent, and the panel's note reads "The microphone stopped: … The picture is still recording." What the microphone wrote lands with the recording.

A [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/#good-to-know) is different. With nothing else recording, it ends there.

## Plug devices in and take them out

The **Camera**, **Format** and **Microphone** lists follow the devices you plug in or take away.

- Changes apply only while the panel is idle, so nothing moves during a countdown, a recording or a landing. A change that waited applies when the panel goes idle.
- A change made while the panel was closed is picked up when it next shows.
- A microphone you take away falls back to **Off**. A camera falls back to the default camera, or to **None connected** when there's no camera left.
- When a device comes back it's chosen again, and a camera comes back with its stored format.
- Plugging in or removing a device doesn't change what the panel remembers. The next control you change saves whatever the lists show at that moment, so a device that's away at that point is forgotten.
- A list is rebuilt only when its own devices changed, so a menu you have open isn't disturbed by an unrelated device.

## With an agent

An agent turns each sound on or off rather than choosing a device. Its microphone is your Mac's default microphone, off unless it asks. It can't ask for the Microphone permission either: that takes one press of **Record** in the panel. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
- [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/)
- [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/)
- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)

---
title: "Start, pause and stop"
description: "Start a recording with its three-second countdown, pause and resume it, stop it from wherever you are, and see what happens if you close the panel or quit."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

This page follows a recording from the press of **Record** to the moment it lands: the countdown, pausing, the places you can stop from, and what Frame Job does if you close the panel or quit along the way.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ New Recording…', 'File ▸ Pause Recording', 'File ▸ Stop Recording']}
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Record', 'The menu-bar item while recording']}
  tools="record_screen"
/>

## Start a recording

<Steps>

1. Set up the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) and press **Record**.

2. Frame Job checks the [permissions](/recording/permissions/) it needs.

3. The panel counts 3, 2, 1, a second each. **Record** reads **Cancel** meanwhile, and the [microphone meter](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/#check-your-level) already moves. Press **Cancel** or close the panel to stop, and nothing is recorded.

4. The recording starts. For a display or a window, the panel leaves the screen and the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) takes over. With **Source** set to **Camera** or **Microphone Only**, nothing on screen is filmed, so the panel stays up.

</Steps>

## What the button says

The panel's main button tells you where the recording has got to.

| The button reads | What's happening | Pressing it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Record** | Nothing yet. | Starts the permission checks and the countdown. |
| **Cancel** | The countdown is running. | Ends it with nothing recorded. |
| **Starting…** | The recording is starting. | It's dimmed. |
| **Stop** | A recording runs or is paused. | Stops and lands it. |
| **Stopping…** | The files are being written. | It's dimmed. |
| **Adding…** | The files are being added to the project. | It's dimmed. |

## If a recording doesn't start

A recording that hasn't started within 20 seconds fails rather than hanging. The panel says "The recording did not start within 20 s." and goes back to **Record**. Any other failed start puts its reason in the same note.

While the button reads **Starting…**, you can still stop with **File ▸ Stop Recording**, or by closing the panel. If Frame Job hadn't begun yet, the note reads "Stopped before the recording began; nothing was recorded." A moment later, it's too late to abandon: the recording ends as soon as it begins, and whatever it caught lands as usual.

## One recording at a time

Only one recording runs at a time. If you press **Record** while another runs or is paused, including one an agent started, the countdown runs and the panel then says "A recording is already in progress."

## Pause and resume

You can pause from any of these:

- the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/)'s **Pause Recording**
- **File ▸ Pause Recording**, directly under **New Recording…**
- the panel's **Pause** button, for a [camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/) or a [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/)

While paused, each of these reads **Resume Recording** or **Resume**. The **File** item is available only while a recording runs or is paused. Pausing has no keyboard shortcut.

On a recording you started, a pause Frame Job can't make beeps, and the recording carries on. A resume that fails leaves it paused, with the reason in the panel's note: at once if the panel is up, otherwise when it comes back after you stop. Try again, or stop and land what you have.

## Paused recordings are stretches

A pause ends the current file and a resume starts a new one, so a paused recording is several stretches. Each stretch has its own movie, and its own microphone, camera and [cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/) when the recording has them.

- Each file is named by the moment its stretch began.
- Each stretch keeps its own width, height and frame rate.
- The paused time is in no file, and the elapsed time counts only what was recorded.

When the recording lands, the stretches sit end to end on one track, touching, with no transition between them. Each stretch's microphone goes on the **Microphone** track, lined up with its own picture.

## Stop a recording

You can stop a running or paused recording from any of these:

- the menu-bar item's **Stop Recording**
- **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>). While any recording runs, **File ▸ New Recording…** reads **Stop Recording**, paused included.
- the panel's **Stop** button, for a camera on its own or a voice-over

Frame Job writes the files and [lands the recording](/recording/where-it-lands/). A clean landing doesn't bring a hidden panel back. Press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> when you want it again.

:::caution
There's no global shortcut to stop. <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> works in Frame Job's own menus, so it does nothing while another app is in front. Use the menu-bar item.
:::

## Stop from macOS's indicator

macOS shows its own indicator in the menu bar during a screen recording, and it can end the recording too. Frame Job keeps what was captured and adds it. The panel's note reads "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added."

## The Welcome window during a recording

The **New Recording…** button on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/) never stops a recording.

- During a screen recording you started in the panel, it only beeps. The panel coming back would put it in the recording.
- During a camera recording or a voice-over, it shows the panel again.

## If the panel closes

A recording carries on if the panel closes, under the menu-bar item and **File ▸ Stop Recording**. You can only do this with a camera on its own or a voice-over, because the panel is off screen for anything else.

Closing it at other moments is different:

- During the countdown, it cancels the countdown and nothing is recorded.
- While the button reads **Starting…**, it counts as a Stop.
- Closing also lets go of a microphone or camera that was warming up for a recording.

## Quit during a recording

Choosing **Quit Frame Job** (<kbd>⌘Q</kbd>) during a recording doesn't quit. It puts the recording's controls in front of you, so you can stop or resume first:

- With the panel hidden for a screen recording, it opens the menu-bar item's menu.
- For a camera recording, a voice-over or an agent's recording, it shows the panel.

Frame Job reviews your unsaved projects before this. If that review closes the project you were recording into, the recording opens as a new project when it lands, and the note says so.

## Stop an agent's recording

A recording an agent starts shows the same menu-bar item, so you can pause, resume or stop it from there or from the **File** menu.

Your Stop ends the agent's recording early, and what was recorded still lands. An agent asks for a length of real time, so a pause shortens what gets recorded rather than extending it. An agent has no way to pause or resume, and it has no countdown. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
- [The menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/)
- [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/)
- [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/)

---
title: "The menu-bar item"
description: "See the elapsed time of a running recording in the menu bar, and pause, resume or stop it from there while another app is in front."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

While a recording runs, Frame Job puts an item in the menu bar. For a display or a window the panel is off screen, so this item is the recording's control, wherever you're working.

<AtAGlance
  where="The menu bar, while a recording runs"
  tools="record_screen"
/>

## What it shows

The item appears when the recording starts, and shows the elapsed time as `m:ss`, then `h:mm:ss` past an hour. Hover over it and its tooltip says which state it's in.

| State | The menu bar shows | Tooltip | Its menu |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Recording | A coral ● and the running time | "Frame Job is recording" | **Pause Recording**, **Stop Recording** |
| Paused | ❚❚ and the time, held still | "Frame Job's recording is paused" | **Resume Recording**, **Stop Recording** |

It needs no permission. It appears for an agent's recording too, so you can [pause or stop one](/recording/pause-and-stop/#stop-an-agents-recording). It comes down the moment the recording ends, before the recording has landed.

## Pause, resume and stop

Click the item for its menu.

- **Pause Recording** pauses. The row then reads **Resume Recording**.
- **Stop Recording** stops the recording, running or paused, and lands it.

The time keeps ticking while the menu is open, so you can read it before you decide. [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/) has the other places to do this. If you choose **Quit Frame Job** while the panel is hidden for a screen recording, Frame Job opens this menu instead of quitting.

## The keyboard mark

While a recording [records shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/), a ⌨︎ mark follows the ● or ❚❚, and the menu starts with a greyed-out **Recording keyboard shortcuts** row. Both show whether the recording is running or paused, and they hold for a recording an agent started with shortcuts on.

## A fixed width

The item is sized once, so the other items in your menu bar don't shift as the seconds tick, when the hours appear, or at a pause. It's sized for times up to 9:59:59, and a little wider when it shows the keyboard mark. Past 9:59:59 the label is wider than that.

## If macOS hides the item

macOS can drop the item from a crowded menu bar or behind the notch. **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **File ▸ Pause Recording** still work, but only with Frame Job in front.

## Related

- [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/)
- [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/)
- [Buttons and context menus](/reference/context-menus/)

---
title: "Record a camera beside the screen"
description: "Record your camera at the same time as a display or a window, for a talking head over a screencast, and choose how it lands."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Tick one box and Frame Job records your camera at the same time as the screen, for a talking head over a screencast. The camera lands as an ordinary clip on a track of its own, already laid out over the screen.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Record the camera too', 'New Recording panel ▸ Layout', "New Recording panel ▸ Remove the camera's background when it lands"]}
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The Screen Recording and Camera permissions, and the Microphone permission when you choose a microphone."
/>

## Record the screen and the camera

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ New Recording…**, and set **Source** to a display or **Window…**.

2. Tick **Record the camera too**. **Camera**, **Format**, **Layout** and **Remove the camera's background when it lands** go live, and a **Preview** of the camera appears under **Format**.

3. Choose the camera in **Camera**, and its size and frame rate in **Format**. [Record a camera](/recording/record-a-camera/) explains both lists.

4. Choose a [layout](#choose-a-layout).

5. Choose a **Microphone** if you want your voice. The camera's movie has no sound of its own.

6. Press **Record**. Frame Job checks its permissions, then counts down from 3.

7. The panel leaves the screen. Pause and stop from the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or the **File** menu.

</Steps>

**Record the camera too** is off until you tick it, and Frame Job remembers it between launches. It's live only with a display or **Window…** as the source. **Camera** and **Microphone Only** grey it out, keeping its value.

**System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows** and **Rate** stay live and apply to the screen, and the note under **Size** describes the screen. The camera records at the frame rate of its **Format**.

### What Record checks

Pressing **Record** stops at the first thing missing, in this order:

1. A camera. With none connected, the panel says "No camera is connected."
2. The Screen Recording permission.
3. The Input Monitoring permission, only with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) ticked.
4. The Camera permission.
5. The Microphone permission, only with a microphone chosen.

[Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/) says what each one asks of you.

### The preview

The camera starts as soon as you tick the box, so it has settled at its frame rate by the time recording begins. Unticking the box, choosing **Microphone Only** or closing the panel turns it off.

The preview shows the chosen camera at the chosen format. When it can't, it says why:

| The preview says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "No camera is connected." | There's no camera to show. |
| "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera." | You haven't allowed the Camera permission yet. Showing the panel never asks for it. Pressing **Record** does. |
| "The camera is recording." | An agent is recording a camera right now. The picture comes back when it ends. |
| Another sentence | The reason the camera couldn't start. Untick and tick the box, or reopen the panel, to try again. |

## Choose a layout

**Layout** sets how the camera sits with the screen when the recording lands.

| Layout | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Corner** | The default. The camera sits in the bottom-right corner, scaled to fit a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % guide of [**View ▸ Safe Areas**](/canvas/safe-areas/). |
| **Rounded Corner** | The same corner with rounded edges. |
| **Circle** | The same corner as a circle. |
| **Side by Side** | The screen and the camera next to each other. |
| **Camera Full** | The camera fills the canvas. |

**Layout** is live only with **Record the camera too** ticked. Otherwise, and while a recording is under way, it's greyed out and keeps its value. Frame Job remembers it between launches.

The panel offers no other corner, no **Stacked** or **Screen Only**, and no scale or inset. [**Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**](/framing/camera-layouts/) has those once the clip has landed. Any crop the panel's layout makes centres on the camera's picture, not on the person.

## The Camera track

When the recording lands, each stretch's camera movie goes on one new track named **Camera**, in front of everything, lined up with that stretch's screen clip. A recording you never paused has one stretch. A paused one has [several](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches).

Frame Job measures how far apart the camera and the screen started, for each stretch. The camera usually starts a moment first, so the clip's first frames are trimmed off rather than the clip starting early. A camera clip never starts before its screen clip, and never overlaps the camera clip before it.

The camera files land in the same undo step as the screen:

| Recording into | The undo step |
| --- | --- |
| An open project | **Add Recording**, for the screen, the camera and any microphone |
| A new project, one stretch | **Add Camera**, or **Add Camera and Microphone** with a microphone. The screen movie is the project itself. |
| A new project, several stretches | **Add Recording Segments** |

[Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) covers the rest of the landing. Each camera file is named after its screen movie with ` (Camera)` added, for example `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov`.

## How far the layout reaches

The layout starts at the camera clip's first frame, so the screen keeps its full picture until the camera arrives. It ends with that stretch's screen clip or its camera clip, whichever is later.

That keeps it to this recording. A clip that was already in the project never moves, and another stretch's screen with no camera of its own stays full.

If a stretch's screen clip is missing, or isn't playing where its camera starts, that camera goes in the bottom-right corner instead, whichever layout you chose.

## Remove the camera's background

Tick **Remove the camera's background when it lands** and Frame Job runs [**Clip ▸ Remove Background**](/effects/remove-background/) on the camera's clips as soon as they land. It works on your Mac, with no key.

The box is off until you tick it, and Frame Job remembers it. It's greyed out, keeping its value, whenever **Layout** is.

It's its own undo step, **Remove Background**, after the landing's and before any [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/) and the **When it lands:** boxes. **Edit ▸ Undo** takes it off and keeps the recording. If no camera clip landed, it does nothing and says nothing.

## Change a camera clip afterwards

Each camera clip stays an ordinary clip. You can move it, or give it another layout from [**Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**](/framing/camera-layouts/) or the [Layout section](/framing/layout-section/).

## Good to know

- If the camera stops on its own during the recording, for example because it's unplugged, the screen keeps recording. What the camera wrote lands, later stretches have no camera, and the panel's note gives the reason. If it stops while the recording is starting, the recording doesn't start.
- A camera clip that would keep less than a frame after its trim goes to the media list without a clip, and a note says so. If no camera clip can be placed, no **Camera** track is added.
- If a stretch is left out because its movie can't be read, its camera file stays on disk and the note names it, but it isn't added to the project.

## With an agent

`record_screen` makes the same recording when it names a camera. An agent can also leave the recording's files in the media list with no clips, which the panel doesn't offer. In that case no **Camera** track is added. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [Record a camera](/recording/record-a-camera/)
- [Camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/)
- [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/)
- [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/)

---
title: "Record a voice-over"
description: "Record narration from your microphone with no picture, at the playhead of the project you're editing or as a new project."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A voice-over is the microphone alone, with no picture. Use it to record narration over your edit: it lands at the playhead, on a new track of its own.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ Source ▸ Microphone Only"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The Microphone permission. Screen Recording isn't needed."
/>

## Record a voice-over

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to where the narration should start.

2. Choose **File ▸ New Recording…**, and set **Source** to **Microphone Only**.

3. Choose your microphone in **Microphone**.

4. Check **Record Into**: the project to land in, or **New Project**.

5. Press **Record**. Frame Job checks the Microphone permission, then counts down from 3.

6. Speak. The panel stays up while you do.

7. Press **Stop**. The button reads **Stopping…** and then **Adding…**, and the voice-over lands. The panel stays up, back on **Record**, ready for another take.

</Steps>

With **Microphone** set to **Off**, **Record** starts nothing and the panel says "Microphone Only records the microphone alone — choose a microphone first."

The controls that only make sense for a picture grey out, keeping their values for next time: **System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows**, **Cursor** and **Record shortcuts**. The note under **Size** reads "no picture — the microphone alone". **Rate** stays live, because it sets the frame rate of a new project.

Frame Job keeps **Microphone Only** in **Source** until you quit, then goes back to your display.

## While it records

Nothing on screen is being filmed, so the panel stays up:

- Its rows are locked.
- The [level meter](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/#check-your-level) stays live.
- The footnote at the bottom left shows ● and the elapsed time, or ❚❚ and the time held still while paused.
- **Record** reads **Stop**, and a **Pause** button stands beside it, reading **Resume** while paused.

The countdown and the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) work as they do for a screen recording, so you can also pause and stop from the menu bar, or from **File ▸ Pause Recording** and **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>).

**Close** takes the panel away and the voice-over carries on. To bring the panel back, click **New Recording…** on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/). <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> won't do it, because it stops the recording.

## Where a voice-over lands

**In an open project,** each [stretch](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches) between pauses is its own file, and they land end to end from the playhead on one new back track named **Microphone**. It's all one undo step, **Add Recording**. If a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) is open, they land inside it.

A voice-over always gets a new track. It never goes on an existing one, even one already named **Microphone**.

**As a new project,** the first file is the project itself, audio only at 1920×1080 and the frame rate in **Rate**. Later files follow it on its one track, as one undo step named **Add Recording Segments**.

Either way they're ordinary audio clips, with everything in the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). To clean your voice up as it lands, tick [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/).

## The files

Each stretch is an `.m4a` file in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by the moment it began, for example `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a`. See [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/).

## Good to know

- If the microphone stops on its own, for example because it's unplugged, the voice-over ends there. What was recorded lands, and the note reads "The microphone stopped recording on its own: … The voice-over ends where it stopped."
- A **Resume** that fails shows its reason in the panel's note, and the voice-over stays paused. Try again, or press **Stop** to land what you have.
- A file too short to fill one frame goes to the media list without a clip, and a note says so. If that's every file, no **Microphone** track is added.
- A project already at its track limit can't take the new track. The files stay on disk and the note names them. See [Limits](/reference/limits/).

## With an agent

`record_screen` records a voice-over too. An agent gets your Mac's default microphone rather than a chosen one, and there's no countdown. It can't pass any of the screen settings with a voice-over. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/)
- [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/)
- [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/)
- [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/)

---
title: "System audio and the microphone"
description: "Record what your Mac plays and your voice as two separate sounds, check your level, and see how the microphone lines up with the picture."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A recording can carry two sounds: what your Mac plays, and your voice. Frame Job keeps them apart, so you can set the level of each on its own after the recording lands.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where={['New Recording panel ▸ System Audio', 'New Recording panel ▸ Microphone']}
  tools="record_screen"
  needs={['System Audio: the Screen Recording permission', 'Microphone: the Microphone permission']}
/>

<Shot
  name="16-recorder-panel.panel"
  alt="The New Recording panel. Microphone is set to Off with a level meter beside it, and the System Audio switch below it is on."
/>

## Record what your Mac plays

**System Audio** records the sound from every app but Frame Job, as the movie's own stereo 48 kHz sound track. It's on until you turn it off, and Frame Job remembers your choice.

With it off, the movie has no sound track at all. The switch applies to the screen, so **Camera** and **Microphone Only** in **Source** grey it out, keeping its value.

## Play the timeline while you record

Frame Job's own sound is never recorded, whether or not **Include Frame Job windows** is on. You can play your timeline during a recording and its sound won't be in the file.

## Record your voice

Choose a microphone in **Microphone**. **Off** comes first and is the default, then every connected microphone by name. Frame Job remembers your choice, and falls back to **Off** if that microphone isn't connected.

It works with every source. The voice goes into a second file beside the movie, named after it with ` (Microphone)` added, and never into the movie. With a chosen microphone, pressing **Record** checks the [Microphone permission](/recording/permissions/) first.

To clean your voice up as it lands, tick [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/). To record your voice with no picture, see [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/).

## Check your level

A meter sits beside **Microphone**. It starts moving at the countdown, not when you choose the microphone, so the 3, 2, 1 is your chance to check your level before the recording starts.

It stays live through the recording, and goes silent while paused. For a display or a window the panel leaves the screen once recording begins, so you only see the meter during the countdown. For a camera on its own or a voice-over, the panel stays up and so does the meter.

## Your first words are kept

The microphone starts during the countdown, not when the recording does, so your first words are in the file. A camera's capture starts early the same way. Both are let go if you cancel the countdown, close the panel, or the start fails.

## How the microphone lands

Each file lands on one new back track named **Microphone**, lined up with its picture, so your voice and the computer's sound have separate volumes.

Frame Job measures how far apart the two files started, for each stretch of a [paused recording](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches) separately, and places the clip to match. The alignment is exact to half a frame.

If your voice started before its clip could, at the very start of the timeline or just after the previous microphone clip, the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip being placed late.

If no voice can be placed, no empty track is added. [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) covers the undo steps.

## If the microphone stops

A microphone that fails doesn't stop a screen or camera recording. The picture keeps going, the meter goes silent, and the panel's note reads "The microphone stopped: … The picture is still recording." What the microphone wrote lands with the recording.

A [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/#good-to-know) is different. With nothing else recording, it ends there.

## Plug devices in and take them out

The **Camera**, **Format** and **Microphone** lists follow the devices you plug in or take away.

- Changes apply only while the panel is idle, so nothing moves during a countdown, a recording or a landing. A change that waited applies when the panel goes idle.
- A change made while the panel was closed is picked up when it next shows.
- A microphone you take away falls back to **Off**. A camera falls back to the default camera, or to **None connected** when there's no camera left.
- When a device comes back it's chosen again, and a camera comes back with its stored format.
- Plugging in or removing a device doesn't change what the panel remembers. The next control you change saves whatever the lists show at that moment, so a device that's away at that point is forgotten.
- A list is rebuilt only when its own devices changed, so a menu you have open isn't disturbed by an unrelated device.

## With an agent

An agent turns each sound on or off rather than choosing a device. Its microphone is your Mac's default microphone, off unless it asks. It can't ask for the Microphone permission either: that takes one press of **Record** in the panel. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
- [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/)
- [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/)
- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)

---
title: "Start, pause and stop"
description: "Start a recording with its three-second countdown, pause and resume it, stop it from wherever you are, and see what happens if you close the panel or quit."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

This page follows a recording from the press of **Record** to the moment it lands: the countdown, pausing, the places you can stop from, and what Frame Job does if you close the panel or quit along the way.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ New Recording…', 'File ▸ Pause Recording', 'File ▸ Stop Recording']}
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Record', 'The menu-bar item while recording']}
  tools="record_screen"
/>

## Start a recording

<Steps>

1. Set up the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) and press **Record**.

2. Frame Job checks the [permissions](/recording/permissions/) it needs.

3. The panel counts 3, 2, 1, a second each. **Record** reads **Cancel** meanwhile, and the [microphone meter](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/#check-your-level) already moves. Press **Cancel** or close the panel to stop, and nothing is recorded.

4. The recording starts. For a display or a window, the panel leaves the screen and the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) takes over. With **Source** set to **Camera** or **Microphone Only**, nothing on screen is filmed, so the panel stays up.

</Steps>

## What the button says

The panel's main button tells you where the recording has got to.

| The button reads | What's happening | Pressing it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Record** | Nothing yet. | Starts the permission checks and the countdown. |
| **Cancel** | The countdown is running. | Ends it with nothing recorded. |
| **Starting…** | The recording is starting. | It's dimmed. |
| **Stop** | A recording runs or is paused. | Stops and lands it. |
| **Stopping…** | The files are being written. | It's dimmed. |
| **Adding…** | The files are being added to the project. | It's dimmed. |

## If a recording doesn't start

A recording that hasn't started within 20 seconds fails rather than hanging. The panel says "The recording did not start within 20 s." and goes back to **Record**. Any other failed start puts its reason in the same note.

While the button reads **Starting…**, you can still stop with **File ▸ Stop Recording**, or by closing the panel. If Frame Job hadn't begun yet, the note reads "Stopped before the recording began; nothing was recorded." A moment later, it's too late to abandon: the recording ends as soon as it begins, and whatever it caught lands as usual.

## One recording at a time

Only one recording runs at a time. If you press **Record** while another runs or is paused, including one an agent started, the countdown runs and the panel then says "A recording is already in progress."

## Pause and resume

You can pause from any of these:

- the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/)'s **Pause Recording**
- **File ▸ Pause Recording**, directly under **New Recording…**
- the panel's **Pause** button, for a [camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/) or a [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/)

While paused, each of these reads **Resume Recording** or **Resume**. The **File** item is available only while a recording runs or is paused. Pausing has no keyboard shortcut.

On a recording you started, a pause Frame Job can't make beeps, and the recording carries on. A resume that fails leaves it paused, with the reason in the panel's note: at once if the panel is up, otherwise when it comes back after you stop. Try again, or stop and land what you have.

## Paused recordings are stretches

A pause ends the current file and a resume starts a new one, so a paused recording is several stretches. Each stretch has its own movie, and its own microphone, camera and [cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/) when the recording has them.

- Each file is named by the moment its stretch began.
- Each stretch keeps its own width, height and frame rate.
- The paused time is in no file, and the elapsed time counts only what was recorded.

When the recording lands, the stretches sit end to end on one track, touching, with no transition between them. Each stretch's microphone goes on the **Microphone** track, lined up with its own picture.

## Stop a recording

You can stop a running or paused recording from any of these:

- the menu-bar item's **Stop Recording**
- **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>). While any recording runs, **File ▸ New Recording…** reads **Stop Recording**, paused included.
- the panel's **Stop** button, for a camera on its own or a voice-over

Frame Job writes the files and [lands the recording](/recording/where-it-lands/). A clean landing doesn't bring a hidden panel back. Press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> when you want it again.

:::caution
There's no global shortcut to stop. <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> works in Frame Job's own menus, so it does nothing while another app is in front. Use the menu-bar item.
:::

## Stop from macOS's indicator

macOS shows its own indicator in the menu bar during a screen recording, and it can end the recording too. Frame Job keeps what was captured and adds it. The panel's note reads "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added."

## The Welcome window during a recording

The **New Recording…** button on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/) never stops a recording.

- During a screen recording you started in the panel, it only beeps. The panel coming back would put it in the recording.
- During a camera recording or a voice-over, it shows the panel again.

## If the panel closes

A recording carries on if the panel closes, under the menu-bar item and **File ▸ Stop Recording**. You can only do this with a camera on its own or a voice-over, because the panel is off screen for anything else.

Closing it at other moments is different:

- During the countdown, it cancels the countdown and nothing is recorded.
- While the button reads **Starting…**, it counts as a Stop.
- Closing also lets go of a microphone or camera that was warming up for a recording.

## Quit during a recording

Choosing **Quit Frame Job** (<kbd>⌘Q</kbd>) during a recording doesn't quit. It puts the recording's controls in front of you, so you can stop or resume first:

- With the panel hidden for a screen recording, it opens the menu-bar item's menu.
- For a camera recording, a voice-over or an agent's recording, it shows the panel.

Frame Job reviews your unsaved projects before this. If that review closes the project you were recording into, the recording opens as a new project when it lands, and the note says so.

## Stop an agent's recording

A recording an agent starts shows the same menu-bar item, so you can pause, resume or stop it from there or from the **File** menu.

Your Stop ends the agent's recording early, and what was recorded still lands. An agent asks for a length of real time, so a pause shortens what gets recorded rather than extending it. An agent has no way to pause or resume, and it has no countdown. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
- [The menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/)
- [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/)
- [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/)

---
title: "The menu-bar item"
description: "See the elapsed time of a running recording in the menu bar, and pause, resume or stop it from there while another app is in front."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

While a recording runs, Frame Job puts an item in the menu bar. For a display or a window the panel is off screen, so this item is the recording's control, wherever you're working.

<AtAGlance
  where="The menu bar, while a recording runs"
  tools="record_screen"
/>

## What it shows

The item appears when the recording starts, and shows the elapsed time as `m:ss`, then `h:mm:ss` past an hour. Hover over it and its tooltip says which state it's in.

| State | The menu bar shows | Tooltip | Its menu |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Recording | A coral ● and the running time | "Frame Job is recording" | **Pause Recording**, **Stop Recording** |
| Paused | ❚❚ and the time, held still | "Frame Job's recording is paused" | **Resume Recording**, **Stop Recording** |

It needs no permission. It appears for an agent's recording too, so you can [pause or stop one](/recording/pause-and-stop/#stop-an-agents-recording). It comes down the moment the recording ends, before the recording has landed.

## Pause, resume and stop

Click the item for its menu.

- **Pause Recording** pauses. The row then reads **Resume Recording**.
- **Stop Recording** stops the recording, running or paused, and lands it.

The time keeps ticking while the menu is open, so you can read it before you decide. [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/) has the other places to do this. If you choose **Quit Frame Job** while the panel is hidden for a screen recording, Frame Job opens this menu instead of quitting.

## The keyboard mark

While a recording [records shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/), a ⌨︎ mark follows the ● or ❚❚, and the menu starts with a greyed-out **Recording keyboard shortcuts** row. Both show whether the recording is running or paused, and they hold for a recording an agent started with shortcuts on.

## A fixed width

The item is sized once, so the other items in your menu bar don't shift as the seconds tick, when the hours appear, or at a pause. It's sized for times up to 9:59:59, and a little wider when it shows the keyboard mark. Past 9:59:59 the label is wider than that.

## If macOS hides the item

macOS can drop the item from a crowded menu bar or behind the notch. **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **File ▸ Pause Recording** still work, but only with Frame Job in front.

## Related

- [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/)
- [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/)
- [Buttons and context menus](/reference/context-menus/)

- A Stop during Starting… gives the "nothing was recorded" note only before Frame Job has handed the attempt to the recorder. After that, the recording ends as soon as it begins and whatever it caught lands.
- The level meter starts moving at the countdown, not while idle, so the guide's "live level meter" is only true from then on.
- The panel's Starting…, Stopping… and Adding… states dim the button. The brief's "it beeps" could not be reached from the button, so the page says it is dimmed.
- During an agent's recording, the Welcome window's New Recording… button and Quit both show the panel. The brief only described the panel's own recordings.
- "No camera clip landed…" is only the agent tool's sentence. The panel says nothing in that case, and the page says so.
- A hot-plugged device isn't forgotten until the next control change, which saves what the lists show at that moment. The page states this exception.
- A camera beside the screen that stops on its own doesn't end the recording; the screen carries on. The page says so.

A stale code comment in RecorderPanelController.swift says that with the panel hidden, Stop survives in the File menu but Pause and Resume do not. File ▸ Pause Recording does exist and works, so the page follows the menu code.
